rv.q: The play, under the lively direction of Guardian critic Brian Logan, is a slippery to-and-fro of strategy, speculation and cunning.

Occasionally, Jamie and Kyla’s conversation slips into imaginary sequences, the most moving of which sees them pretend they are successful artists in an alternate universe. Yes, teenagers today can be deeply troubled, the play observes, but amid the mayhem, they are also ambitious, clever and compassionate.
